subject: PE & Wellbeing
source: National Curriculum (Physical Education); UK Chief Medical Officers' physical activity guidelines. Drive PE folder reviewed (TSS Long-Term PE Plan: fitness, fair play, leadership, resilience) and adapted to at-home, no-equipment, no-contact lessons.

lessons.title: Health-related components of fitness
objectives: Define the five health-related components of fitness
Complete a baseline fitness test safely

keywords.def: how well your heart and lungs supply muscles with oxygen
the most force a muscle can make
how long a muscle can keep working
the range of movement at a joint
the proportion of fat, muscle and bone in the body

starter: Bismillah. What is the daily activity guideline?

teach.heading: Safety first
bullets: Stop if you feel pain, dizziness or sickness
teach.note: Read this slide aloud every lesson. Parents are asked to confirm their child is well enough to take part and to tell the school about any medical condition (e.g. asthma: inhaler within reach). No contact activities in any TGA online PE lesson.

teach.heading: Five components
teach.note: Define each simply. Misconception: body composition is the same as weight; it is about what the body is made of. Handle body image with care; do not weigh pupils.

teach.heading: Matching tests
bullets: Cardio: jog on the spot for 3 minutes, then check pulse
teach.note: Choose bodyweight tests that need no equipment. Keep results private; no pupil reports to the group.

teach.heading: Muscular endurance
teach.note: Offer kneeling and incline variations. Stop at good technique failing.

teach.heading: Interpreting results
teach.note: Goals are about personal progress. A SMART target is specific, measurable, achievable, realistic and time-bound. Link to the hadith that the strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, while there is good in both (Sahih Muslim).

practice: Which component does a plank train?
independent: Match six exercises to their main component.
Carry out the squat test and record it.
exit: Complete three baseline tests and record results in a table.
Set one SMART target for four weeks.
lessons.send: Choose a baseline test and repeat it at the end of the week to check technique.

lessons.title: Bodyweight strength: squat, lunge, press-up
objectives: Perform the squat, lunge and press-up with correct technique

keywords.def: the correct way to perform an exercise
one complete movement of an exercise
the large muscles at the front of the thigh

teach.heading: Safety first
bullets: Do not lock joints or bounce
Stop if you feel sharp pain
teach.note: Read this slide aloud every lesson. Parents are asked to confirm their child is well enough to take part and to tell the school about any medical condition (e.g. asthma: inhaler within reach). No contact activities in any TGA online PE lesson.

teach.heading: Squat
teach.note: Model from front and side. Misconception: knees must not go past toes at all; the key is control and comfortable depth. Quadriceps and glutes work.

teach.heading: Lunge
teach.note: Use a wall for balance if needed. Alternate legs. Pupils may do split-stance static lunges.

teach.heading: Press-up variations
teach.note: Body in a straight line from shoulders to knees or heels. Pupils choose the level where technique stays good.

teach.heading: Programme a set
teach.note: Explain that it is safer to build slowly. Include stretching afterwards.

practice: Name the muscles in the front of the thigh.
How many reps are in a set of ten?
independent: Do 5 lunges each leg with support.
exit: Complete two sets of squats, lunges and a press-up variation.
Write a technique tip for each exercise.
homework: What is the correct depth of a squat?
Which press-up variation would you start with?
lessons.send: Do your strength set twice this week on non-consecutive days.
